text:
The coefficient of $x^{7}$
 in the expression 

$(1 + x)^{10} + x(1 + x)^{9}$
 $+ x^{2}(1 + x)^{8}$
 $+ ......+ x^{10}$ is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$(1 + x)^{10} + x(1 + x)^{9}$
 $+ x^{2}(1 + x)^{8}$
 $+ ......+ x^{10}$

This is a G.P where

First term, $a = (1 + x)^{10}$

common ratio, r = $\frac{x}{1+x}$

Number of terms = 11

Sum of G.P

= $\frac{(1+x)^{10}\left (1-\left (\frac{x}{1+x}\right )^{11}\right )}{1-\frac{x}{1+x}}$

$=  (1 + x)^{11}$
 $– x^{11}$

So Coefficient of $x^{7}$
 is $^{11}C_{7} = 330$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot

text:
Let y = y(x) be the solution curve of the differential equation,

$\left (y^{2}-x\right )\frac{dy}{dx}=1$, satisfying y(0) =
1. This curve intersects the x-axis at a point whose abscissa is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\left (y^{2}-x\right )\frac{dy}{dx}=1$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{dx}{dy}$ $+ x = y^{2}$

I.F = $e^{\int dy}$ $= e^{y}$

Solution is given by

$xe^{y} =$ $\int y^{2}e^{y}dy$

$\Rightarrow$ $xe^{y} = (y^{2} – 2y + 2)e^{y} + C$

y(0) = 1 means x = 0, y = 1

$\therefore$ C = -e

$\therefore$ $xe^{y} = (y^{2} – 2y + 2)e^{y} - e$

put y = 0

$\therefore$ x = 0 – 0 + 2 – e

$\Rightarrow$ x = 2 - e
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot

text:
The locus of the mid-points of the perpendiculars drawn from points on the line, x = 2y to the line
x = y is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
[IMG]


Slope of line y = x is 1

Line AB is perpendicular to line y = x so

Slope of AB = -1

Also slope of AB = $\frac{α-β}{2α-β}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{α-β}{2α-β}$ = -1

$\Rightarrow$ 3$α$ = 2$β$

h = $\frac{2α+β}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ 2h = $\frac{4α+2β}{2}$ = $\frac{4α+3α}{2}$ = $\frac{7α}{2}$

Also k = $\frac{α+β}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ 2k = $\frac{5α}{2}$

So $\frac{h}{k}=\frac{7}{5}$

$\Rightarrow$ 5h = 7k 

$\Rightarrow$ 5x = 7y

text:
Let y = y(x) be a function of x satisfying 

$y\sqrt{1-x^{2}}=k-x\sqrt{1-y^{2}}$ where k is a constant and

$y\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )=-\frac{1}{4}$. Then $\frac{dy}{dx}$ at x = $\frac{1}{2}$, is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$y\sqrt{1-x^{2}}=k-x\sqrt{1-y^{2}}$ ....(1)

On differentiating both side of eq. (1) w.r.t. x we
get,

$\frac{dy}{dx}\sqrt{1-x^{2}}-y\frac{2x}{2\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}$

= 0 - $\sqrt{1-y^{2}}+\frac{xy}{\sqrt{1-y^{2}}}\frac{dy}{dx}$

Put x = $\frac{1}{2}$ and y = $-\frac{1}{4}$, we get

$\frac{dy}{dx}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\left (-\frac{1}{4}\right )\frac{\frac{1}{2}}{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}$

= $-\frac{\sqrt{15}}{4}+\frac{-\frac{1}{8}}{\frac{\sqrt{15}}{4}}.\frac{dy}{dx}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot

text:
If $θ_{1}$
 and $θ_{2}$
 be respectively the smallest and the largest values of $θ$ in (0, 2$π$) - {$π$} which satisfy
the equation,

$2\cot ^{2}θ$ - $\frac{5}{\sin θ}$ + 4 = 0, then

$\int\limits _{θ_{1}}^{θ_{2}}\cos ^{2}3θdθ$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$2\cot ^{2}θ$ - $\frac{5}{\sin θ}$ + 4 = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $2\frac{\cos ^{2}θ}{\sin ^{2}θ}-\frac{5}{\sin θ}+4$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $2\sin ^{2}$
$θ$ – 5sin$θ$ + 2 = 0
 

$\Rightarrow$ (2sin$θ$ – 1)(sin$θ$ – 2) = 0

$\therefore$ sin$θ$ = $\frac{1}{2}$ [ sin$θ$ = 2 not possible]

$\therefore$ $θ_{1}$ = $\frac{π}{6}$ and $θ_{2}$ = $\frac{5π}{6}$ as $θ_{1}$ $<$ $θ_{2}$

$\therefore$ I = $\int\limits _{\frac{π}{6}}^{\frac{5π}{6}}\cos ^{2}3θdθ$

= $\int\limits _{\frac{π}{6}}^{\frac{5π}{6}}\frac{1+\cos 6θ}{2}dθ$

= $\frac{1}{2}\left [θ+\frac{\sin 6θ}{2}\right ]_{\frac{π}{6}}^{\frac{5π}{6}}$

= $\frac{π}{3}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot

text:
If $\frac{3+i\sin θ}{4-i\cos θ}$, $θ$ $\in$ [0, 2$π$], is a real number, then an argument of 
sin$θ$ + icos$θ$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let z = $\frac{3+i\sin θ}{4-i\cos θ}$

= $\frac{3+i\sin θ}{4-i\cos θ}\times \frac{(4+i\cos θ)}{(4+i\cos θ)}$

= $\frac{(12-\sin θ\cos θ)+i(4\sin θ+3\cos θ)}{16+\cos ^{2}θ}$

As Z is purely real

$\therefore$ 4sin$θ$ + 3cos$θ$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ tan $θ$ = $-\frac{3}{4}$

$\therefore$ $θ$ lies in the $2^{nd}$ quadrant then 

arg(sinθ + icosθ) = $π$ + $\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{\cos θ}{\sin θ}\right )$

= $π-\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{4}{3}\right )$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot

text:
Let ƒ(x) be a polynomial of degree 5 such that x = ±1 are its critical points.

If $\lim _{x\to 0}\left (2+\frac{f(x)}{x^{3}}\right )=4$, then which one of the following is not true?
options: x = 1 is a point of minima and x = -1 is a point of maxima of ƒ.
x = 1 is a point of maxima and x = -1 is a point of minimum of ƒ.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
let $f(x) = ax^{5} + bx^{4} + cx^{3} + dx^{2} + ex + f$

Given $\lim _{x\to 0}\left (2+\frac{f(x)}{x^{3}}\right )=4$

$\Rightarrow$ $\lim _{x\to 0}\left (2+\frac{ax^{5}+bx^{4}+cx^{3}+dx^{2}+ex+f}{x^{3}}\right )$ = 4

As this limit exists so d = e = f = 0

$\therefore$ $f(x) = ax^{5} + bx^{4} + cx^{3}$

$\lim _{x\to 0}\left (2+\frac{ax^{5}+bx^{4}+cx^{3}}{x^{3}}\right )$ = 4

$\Rightarrow$ 2 + c = 4

$\Rightarrow$ c = 2

$\therefore$ $f(x) = ax^{5} + bx^{4} + 2x^{3}$

$\Rightarrow$ $f'(x) = 5ax^{4} + 4bx^{3} + 6x^{2}$

As x = ±1 are its critical points so f'(x) = 0 at x = ±1.

f'(1) = 5a + 4b + 6 = 0 ....(1)

and f'(-1) = 5a - 4b + 6 = 0 .....(2)

Solving (1) and (2),

a = $-\frac{6}{5}$ and b = 0

$\therefore$ f(x) = $-\frac{6}{5}x^{5}+2x^{3}$

So $f'(x) = -6x^{4} +  6x^{2} = 6x^{2}(1 + x)(1 - x)$

 Sign scheme for f'(x)


[IMG]


It is clear that maxima at x = 1 and minima at x
= –1.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Direction Ratio of PQ are

= ($\frac{5}{3}-1$, $\frac{7}{3}-0$, $\frac{17}{3}-3$)

= (2, 7, 8)

Direction ratio of line QA are

= ($α-\frac{5}{3}$, $7-\frac{7}{3}$, 1 - $\frac{17}{3}$)

= (3$α$ – 5, 14, –14)

PQ is perpendicular to line QA

$\therefore$ $PQ\leftarrow .QA\leftarrow$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ 2(3$α$ – 5) + 7.14 + (–14).8 = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $α$ = 4

text:
If the system of linear equations,

x + y + z = 6

x + 2y + 3z = 10

3x + 2y + $λ$z = $μ$

has more than two solutions, then $μ$ - $λ^{2}$
 is equal to $______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given system of equation more than
2 solutions.
Hence system of equation has infinite many
solution.

$\therefore$ $\Delta$ = $\Delta_{1}$ = $\Delta_{2}$ = $\Delta_{3}$ = 0

$\Delta$ = $\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 2 & λ \end{array}\right |$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ 1(2λ – 6) – 1(λ – 9) + 1(– 4) = 0

$\Rightarrow$ 2λ – 6 – λ + 9 – 4 = 0

$\Rightarrow$ λ = 1

$\Delta_{1}$ = $\left |\begin{array}{lll} 6 & 1 & 1 \\ 10 & 2 & 3 \\ μ & 2 & λ \end{array}\right |$ = 0

 6(2λ – 6) – 1(10λ – 3μ) + 1(20 – 2μ) = 0

$\Rightarrow$ 12λ – 36 – 10λ + 3μ + 20 – 2μ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ 2λ + μ = 16

$\Rightarrow$ 2 + μ = 16

$\Rightarrow$ $μ$ = 14

 $\therefore$ $μ$ - $λ^{2}$ = 14 - 1 = 13
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot

text:
If the function ƒ defined on $\left (-\frac{1}{3},\frac{1}{3}\right )$ by

f(x) = $\left \{\begin{array}{ll} \frac{1}{x}\log _{e}\left (\frac{1+3x}{1-2x}\right ), & whenx\neq 0 \\ k, & whenx=0 \end{array} \right.$

is continuous, then
k is equal $to_______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\lim _{x\to 0}f(x)$

= $\lim _{x\to 0}\left (\frac{\ln (1+3x)}{x}-\frac{\ln (1-2x)}{x}\right )$

= $\lim _{x\to 0}\left (3\frac{\ln (1+3x)}{3x}-(-2)\frac{\ln (1-2x)}{-2x}\right )$

= 3 + 2 = 5

f(x) is continuous

$\therefore$ $\lim _{x\to 0}f(x)$ = f(0)

So f(0) = 5 = k
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Evening Slot
